boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Saint Mary’s spaces for studying, gathering, meals, activity, and quiet reflection.

cards.title: Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus common meeting place
cards.notes: Start here when you need a central indoor meeting point: the building combines student organizations, meeting rooms, an atrium, dining access, and campus services.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub that brings organizations, services, meeting rooms, and dining together.
cards.evidence_claim: The College catalog describes the Student Center as a common meeting place and lists meeting rooms, a large atrium, student-organization offices, services, and dining access.
cards.source_title: Campus and Buildings | Saint Mary's College, Notre Dame, IN
cards.access_notes: Use campus access guidance and any event or room-reservation requirements.

cards.title: Rice Commons
cards.subtitle: Inside the Student Center
cards.notes: Use this named Student Center space as a waypoint when coordinating with classmates or campus offices; confirm any event setup or reservation needs before planning a gathering.
cards.short_summary: A named commons within the Student Center’s mix of student-facing spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The College catalog lists Rice Commons among the spaces in the Student Center.
cards.source_title: Campus and Buildings | Saint Mary's College, Notre Dame, IN
cards.access_notes: Located in the Student Center; availability may vary with campus programming.

cards.title: Noble Family Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Student Center dining hall
cards.notes: Plan a meal or a seated catch-up here, then use the Student Center’s nearby common areas for conversation. Check current campus dining eligibility and service details.
cards.short_summary: The College’s named dining hall, entered through the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The College catalog identifies Noble Family Dining Hall as part of the Student Center and notes that the Student Center is its entrance.
cards.source_title: Campus and Buildings | Saint Mary's College, Notre Dame, IN
cards.access_notes: Food service may require a meal plan, Flex Points, or another payment method.

cards.title: Vander Vennet Theatre
cards.subtitle: Student Center performance venue
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar for a show or presentation, and arrive through the Student Center. Treat it as an event venue rather than an always-open lounge.
cards.short_summary: A named theatre in the Student Center for scheduled performances and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: The campus map lists Vander Vennet Theatre as a performance venue in the Student Center.
cards.access_notes: Attend during scheduled events; ticketing or reservations may apply.

cards.title: Cushwa-Leighton Library
cards.subtitle: Library study and research spaces
cards.notes: Choose a quiet workstation for solo work or reserve a group room when collaborating. The library also puts academic support and technology resources in the same building.
cards.short_summary: A library with individual workstations, group rooms, research help, and student-centered spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says Cushwa-Leighton Library has reservable group study rooms and quiet individual workstations throughout the building.
cards.access_notes: Group study rooms are reservable; follow library access and reservation policies.

cards.title: Trumper Computer Center
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Cushwa-Leighton Library
cards.notes: Use the lower-level computer center for a focused computer-based work session, especially when you need campus printing or access to installed academic software.
cards.short_summary: A library computer center with student access around the clock during the school year.
cards.evidence_claim: The College catalog states that the Trumper Computer Center is in the lower level of Cushwa-Leighton Library and offers students 24-hour access when classes are in session.
cards.source_title: Campus and Buildings | Saint Mary's College, Notre Dame, IN
cards.access_notes: 24-hour student access is stated for times when classes are in session; verify current building access rules.

cards.title: Center for Academic Innovation
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Cushwa-Leighton Library
cards.notes: Bring a partner or project group to this flexible third-floor space for study, meetings, or socializing, and check its programming before relying on a specific setup.
cards.short_summary: A flexible Learning Commons space for meetings, study, and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s describes the Center for Academic Innovation as a flexible space for faculty and student meetings, study space, and socializing on the library’s third floor.
cards.source_title: Center for Academic Innovation | Saint Mary's College
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Cushwa-Leighton Library; programming may affect availability.

cards.title: Niner’s Lounge
cards.subtitle: McCandless Hall
cards.notes: If you live in McCandless, use this renovated lounge for a small study session, cooking, or gathering. Respect residence-hall guest and kitchen policies.
cards.short_summary: A renovated McCandless lounge designed for cooking, gathering, and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that Niner’s Lounge in McCandless Hall was renovated to create spaces to cook, gather, and study.
cards.access_notes: Residential space; access is subject to residence-life and guest policies.

cards.title: Angela Athletic & Wellness Complex
cards.subtitle: Recreation, fitness, and social areas
cards.notes: Build a movement break around the field house, track, or fitness spaces, then regroup in the café and social area. Confirm facility access and program schedules first.
cards.short_summary: A recreation and wellness complex with fitness spaces and a social area.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s lists a three-court field house, elevated track, fitness-class spaces, café, and social area among Angela’s facilities.
cards.source_title: Belles Athletics & Sports | Saint Mary's College
cards.access_notes: Facility access and fitness offerings may be scheduled or restricted to eligible users.

cards.title: Holy Spirit Chapel
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Le Mans Hall
cards.notes: Stop by for quiet reflection or worship in this chapel on Le Mans Hall’s third floor. Keep the setting contemplative and follow any posted worship guidance.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus chapel that the College describes as open around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says Holy Spirit Chapel is on the third floor of Le Mans Hall and is open 24 hours a day for students’ reflection and worship.
cards.source_title: Holy Spirit Chapel Celebrates its Centennial | Saint Mary's College
cards.access_notes: The College describes the chapel as open 24 hours daily; observe quiet and any posted religious-service guidance.

cards.title: Attend Raise Your Voice programming

cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s listed the April 13, 2026 Raise Your Voice Symposium as free and open to the public.

cards.title: Watch Dance Performance Finals

cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s stated that its 2026 Dance Performance Finals event was free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The cited 2026 finals were free and open to the public; confirm venue and date for future finals.

cards.title: Catch a String Ensemble concert
cards.subtitle: Stapleton Lounge, Le Mans Hall
cards.notes: Use the Moreau Marquee to find the next String Ensemble date and settle in for an evening concert with no admission charge.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Mary’s String Ensemble performance in Stapleton Lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s stated that admission for its listed String Ensemble performance was free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The cited performance was free and open to the public; confirm future performance details before going.

cards.title: Listen to the Spring Choir Concert
cards.subtitle: Church of Our Lady of Loretto
cards.notes: Look for the spring concert announcement, then gather a few people for a choral program inside the Church of Our Lady of Loretto.
cards.short_summary: A choral concert featuring Saint Mary’s singing groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s stated that admission for its listed Spring Choir Concert was free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The cited concert was free and open to the public; confirm the current spring program before attending.

cards.title: Go to a flute and piano recital
cards.subtitle: Stapleton Lounge, Le Mans Hall
cards.notes: Check the Marquee for a recital date, then use the set time to hear faculty or guest musicians in a small campus venue.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Mary’s music recital in Stapleton Lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s stated that admission for its listed Flute and Piano Recital was free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The cited recital was free and open to the public; verify the current recital listing before attending.

cards.entity_name: Anne Lindberg: At the Edge of the Sea
cards.title: View a Moreau Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: Moreau Art Galleries, Moreau Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition dates, then spend time looking closely at the work and comparing observations with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art exhibition presented through the Moreau Art Galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s described the Moreau Galleries as venues for professional contemporary-art exhibitions and listed Anne Lindberg’s 2026 exhibition there.
cards.access_notes: Saint Mary’s separately states that Moreau Art Gallery events are free and open to the public; confirm the current exhibition’s access details.

cards.entity_name: George and Juanda Bick Nature Area Trail
cards.title: Walk the Bick Nature Area trail
cards.subtitle: George and Juanda Bick Nature Area, adjacent to campus
cards.notes: Follow the two-and-a-half-mile trail at an unhurried pace; bring water, stay on the route, and leave plants and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A trail through Saint Mary’s 100-acre nature area beside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s describes the adjacent George and Juanda Bick Nature Area as a 100-acre area with a two-and-a-half-mile trail for looking, listening, studying, contemplating, and photographing.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase requirement is stated on the College’s nature-area page; follow its no-hunting, no-collecting, no-smoking guidance.

warnings: Several cited College event pages document specific 2026 offerings that have already occurred as of the supplied fetch date; verify future dates before visiting.
The Bick Nature Area page documents the trail and permitted enjoyment but does not explicitly state an admission policy.

cards.title: Trumper Computer Cluster
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Cushwa-Leighton Library

cards.short_summary: A 24-hour computer cluster in the library’s lower level.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s identifies the Trumper Computer Cluster in the lower level as a 24-hour study space.
cards.access_notes: Saint Mary’s describes this cluster as 24-hour; confirm building access requirements and current operations before going.

cards.title: Writing and Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Cushwa-Leighton Library
cards.notes: Schedule or walk in for a writing-focused session, then bring your draft and assignment details to work through the next revision.
cards.short_summary: The library’s third-floor site for in-person writing support.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that in-person Writing and Learning Center appointments take place on the third floor of Cushwa-Leighton Library.

cards.access_notes: In-person tutoring is offered on a scheduled or walk-in basis; appointments are made through the College’s scheduling platform.

cards.title: Center for Academic Innovation Space
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Cushwa-Leighton Library
cards.notes: Use this third-floor space next to the Writing and Learning Center when your work includes an in-person tutoring appointment.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor library space beside the Writing and Learning Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s lists the Center for Academic Innovation Space next to the Writing and Learning Center on the third floor of Cushwa-Leighton Library.
cards.source_title: What We Do | Saint Mary's College
cards.access_notes: The College identifies this as a location for in-person Writing and Learning Center appointments; use the scheduling platform for appointment details.

cards.title: Rare Book Room
cards.subtitle: Lowest level, Cushwa-Leighton Library
cards.notes: Plan a source-driven research session around the room’s rare materials, and check with library staff for appropriate use arrangements first.

cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s reports that the Rare Book Room on the library’s lowest level contains more than 4,300 items and offers students opportunities to engage with rare books and manuscripts.

cards.title: McCandless Hall Study Carrels

cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that every McCandless resident is assigned a shared, air-conditioned study carrel with a desk and chair.
cards.access_notes: For McCandless residents; the College says each resident is assigned a shared carrel.

cards.title: Niner's Lounge
cards.subtitle: McCandless Hall
cards.notes: For a change from a desk carrel, settle into Niner’s Lounge and use its renovated common area for reading or group prep.
cards.short_summary: A renovated McCandless common space designated for gathering and study.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says Niner’s Lounge in McCandless was renovated to create spaces to cook, gather, and study.
cards.access_notes: Located in McCandless Hall; residence-hall access may be limited to residents and authorized guests.

cards.title: Reignbeaux Lounge

cards.notes: Bring a partner or a small project to the first-floor tables, which Saint Mary’s specifically describes for studying and meeting.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Le Mans lounge with large study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that Reignbeaux Lounge is on Le Mans Hall’s first floor and has large tables where students can study and meet.
cards.source_title: Le Mans Hall | Saint Mary's College

cards.title: Stapleton Lounge

cards.short_summary: A Le Mans common area described by the College as quieter for study.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says Stapleton Lounge often provides a quieter atmosphere for study and also hosts hall programs.
cards.source_title: Le Mans Hall | Saint Mary's College
cards.access_notes: Located within Le Mans Hall and may host hall programs; residence-hall access may be limited to residents and authorized guests.

cards.title: Regina Hall North Lounge
cards.subtitle: Regina Hall
cards.notes: Use the north lounge for an individual work block or coordinated group session, taking advantage of the space’s study-oriented furnishings.
cards.short_summary: One of Regina’s named lounges for individual or group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s identifies Regina Hall’s north lounge as a space with options for individual or group work.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Saint Mary’s College rituals, landmarks, and annual milestones.

cards.title: Close the Circle
cards.subtitle: First-year orientation tradition
cards.notes: During orientation, join your incoming class for this ceremonial gathering that marks the beginning of its shared Saint Mary’s experience.
cards.short_summary: A first-year class ritual held during orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s identifies Closing the Circle as an orientation event for first-year students that signifies coming together as a class.
cards.access_notes: Participation is part of incoming-student orientation; confirm orientation details with the College.

cards.title: Open the Circle
cards.subtitle: Senior Week tradition
cards.notes: See the senior class revisit the circle during Senior Week, using the ceremony to mark departure from the College community.
cards.short_summary: A Senior Week counterpart to the first-year circle ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that seniors attend Opening the Circle during Senior Week as a symbol of leaving the College to make a difference in the world.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors during Senior Week; consult College communications for program details.

cards.title: Take the First Walk
cards.subtitle: Orientation on The Avenue
cards.notes: At orientation, walk The Avenue with your class while family and friends cheer the first official passage through this campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: New students’ ceremonial first trip down The Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says family and friends cheer students during their first official walk down The Avenue at Orientation.
cards.access_notes: An orientation activity for incoming students; follow the College’s orientation schedule.

cards.title: Make the Last Walk
cards.subtitle: Senior Week on The Avenue
cards.notes: During Senior Week, follow the mirrored route down The Avenue as faculty and staff cheer the class through its final campus walk.
cards.short_summary: Graduating students’ final ceremonial walk down The Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s documents a final walk down The Avenue during Senior Week, with faculty and staff cheering students on.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors during Senior Week; follow the College’s published schedule.

cards.title: Wear the Saint Mary’s Ring
cards.subtitle: Junior-year class-ring tradition
cards.notes: If you choose to purchase one in junior year, look closely at the Ring’s Spes Unica motto, French cross, and Holy Cross anchors.
cards.short_summary: The College’s distinctive class ring links Belles across generations.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says juniors may purchase its class ring, whose design includes Spes Unica, the French cross, and anchors from Holy Cross and College seals.
cards.access_notes: Optional junior-year purchase; obtain current ordering and pricing details directly from the College.

cards.title: Climb the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Le Mans Hall; Senior Week and Reunion
cards.notes: Plan for the limited Bell Tower tour window offered in Senior Week, then return for a Reunion visit when the tower opens again.
cards.short_summary: A landmark tower visit reserved for Senior Week and Reunion.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s states that students tour the Bell Tower during Senior Week and when they return for Reunion.
cards.access_notes: Tours are limited to Senior Week and Reunion periods according to the College; verify availability before planning.

cards.title: Stay for Senior Week
cards.subtitle: The week before Commencement
cards.notes: For graduating students, use the week before Commencement to take part in the College’s planned class activities and milestone ceremonies.
cards.short_summary: A full pre-Commencement week reserved for graduating seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s describes Senior Week as a full week of activities for seniors after other students leave campus and before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors immediately before Commencement; activity details vary by year.

cards.title: Leave a Handprint
cards.subtitle: Senior Week tunnel tradition
cards.notes: During Senior Week, add your handprint only through the College-organized class opportunity, contributing to the designated tunnel section with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A class handprint ritual that marks seniors’ contribution to Saint Mary’s.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says each class can fill a tunnel section with handprints during Senior Week as a symbol of having a hand in shaping the College.
cards.access_notes: Participate only through the Senior Week class activity and in the section designated by the College.

cards.title: Attend a Madrigal Dinner
cards.subtitle: Annual Department of Music holiday event
cards.notes: Attend the annual Renaissance-style holiday dinner and performance, where courses are announced with fanfare and song amid seasonal entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Mary’s Christmas banquet-performance tradition dating to 1972.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s says its Department of Music has presented an annual Christmas Madrigal Dinner since 1972, with a Renaissance-style banquet and performance.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult the Department of Music or College events calendar for current tickets and timing.

cards.title: Mark Founders’ Day
cards.subtitle: October 13 College observance
cards.notes: Use the October observance to learn about Father Sorin, Mother Angela Gillespie, and Basil Moreau, figures central to Saint Mary’s founding.
cards.short_summary: An annual observance of Saint Mary’s founding and its co-founders.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Mary’s style guidance states that Founders’ Day is traditionally celebrated October 13 and honors Father Edward Sorin, Mother Angela Gillespie, and Blessed Basil Anthony Moreau.
cards.access_notes: Traditionally observed October 13; check College announcements for any current campus programming.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Saint Mary's College, Shared as Cards

cards.notes: Use the official campus map to find Le Mans Hall, then trace the nearby library, Student Center, Lake Marian, and arts buildings before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A map-based first stop for learning the campus layout.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Saint Mary's campus map identifies Le Mans Hall and nearby campus destinations.
cards.access_notes: Use the current official campus map and follow posted building-access guidance.

cards.title: Take a Lake Marian reset
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · a quiet outdoor pause
cards.notes: Walk to Lake Marian after your orientation loop and pause at the water before continuing toward the library or Student Center.
